areas.title: Call for Papers

items.reasoning: The builder clearly supports the required capability: the 'Abstract Information' step of the DevFlow Conf 2027 CFP shows fields of three distinct types — 'Session Title' (text), 'Abstract' (textarea), 'Track' and 'Format' (dropdown) — each with a toggleable 'Required' checkbox, and the two screenshots differ only in Track's required flag being turned on, showing the flag is editable and the form auto-saves ('Saved 16:24:53'). Required-field validation is also demonstrably enforced on a public form: on the seeded AI.Engineer CFP, clicking Next with empty fields produced inline errors 'Description is required', 'Format is required', 'Tags is required', 'Track is required'. Gap: the newly-built DevFlow form was never opened publicly (CFP-S1 hit the turn limit at the Participant step), so the round-trip of newly added custom fields ('Key takeaway' text, 'Audience level' dropdown with 3 options) onto the public form was never observed — the validation evidence comes from a pre-seeded form, not from fields the organizer just created.
evidence_refs: obs: Required-field validation confirmed: clicking Next with Description/Format/Tags/Track empty shows inline alert messages

items.reasoning: Conditional visibility works in both directions on the public form: selecting Format='Workshop' revealed 'Room Setup Requirements' and 'Prerequisites' ('What should attendees know or install beforehand?'), and switching back to Format='Talk' hid both again — confirmed by the agent's snapshots at turns 14–23 and the recorded observation, with dedicated screenshots taken for each state. The builder additionally exposes a per-field 'Logic' control, indicating the show-when configuration is a first-class feature. A related inconsistency (the edit-submission page renders these workshop-only fields regardless of format) is a separate defect and does not affect the create-form behaviour scored here.
evidence_refs: obs: Conditional field logic confirmed: selecting Format=Workshop reveals 'Room Setup Requirements' and 'Prerequisites' ... Switching Format back to 'Talk' hides both fields again

items.reasoning: A public portal URL (/submit/ai-engineer-sandbox-event/form0000-...) loads a branded wizard showing the event name ('AI.Engineer NYC — Call for Speakers 2026', with 'AI.Engineer Sandbox Event – NYC' in the page title), an explicit deadline banner ('Form submissions will be accepted until September 15 at 11:59 PM PDT'), a welcome body listing the tracks ('Agents, Evals, RAG & Retrieval, Infra & Serving and AI in Production. Submissions close September 15, 2026'), and the submission step exposes selectable Track and Format dropdowns matching that configuration. However, the browser session was already authenticated as ada@example.com throughout ('Signed in as ada@example.com'), so no-login reachability was never actually demonstrated in a logged-out context — the wizard's step-2 'Account' step implies anonymous entry is supported but this was not verified.
evidence_refs: obs: The public CFP form's Account step shows "Signed in as ada@example.com..."

items.reasoning: Neither the close-date change nor a logged-out closed portal was ever exercised: CFP-S1 hit the 70-turn limit before reaching the form's settings step, and CFP-S4 was consumed fighting the broken admin grid. There is indirect evidence the concept exists — the organizer dashboard's 'YOUR FORMS' panel labels one form 'closed · closes Jul 31, 2026' versus others 'open' — but no logged-out portal was loaded in a closed state, so the enforcement behaviour cannot be decided.

Submission, confirmation and dashboard listing are all solidly evidenced: the fixture proposal 'Taming 40-Minute CI: Incremental Builds at Monorepo Scale' was submitted and produced an on-screen confirmation ('Submission received — SESS-10 / Thanks for your proposal! ...'), and the speaker portal 'My Submissions' page lists SESS-10 and SESS-15 with explicit status chips ('Pending'), plus SESS-1 'Accepted' and SESS-4 'Withdrawn'. The gap is account creation: the portal session was pre-authenticated as a fixed demo identity (Ada Lovelace, email field disabled/non-editable), so 'a speaker can create a submitter account from the portal' was never exercised or verified.
evidence_refs: obs: Confirmation screen exact wording: 'Submission received — SESS-10' ...
obs: The pre-authenticated speaker identity is fixed as 'Ada Lovelace' (ada@example.com) — email field is disabled/non-editable

items.reasoning: Data round-trips intact. The organizer dashboard's 'RECENT SUBMISSIONS' table lists both fixture proposals — SESS-15 'Your AI Pair Programmer Is Lying to You: Verification Patterns That Scale' (pending, AI in Production, Ada Lovelace) and SESS-10 'Taming 40-Minute CI: Incremental Builds at Monorepo Scale' (pending, Ada Lovelace). The admin submission detail for SESS-10 shows Title, full Description including the speaker-entered key-takeaway sentence, Format 'Talk', Tags 'Production', Track 'Infra & Serving' (the app's closest equivalent to the fixture track), Level 'Intermediate', and the speaker participant — matching what was entered on the public form; the API payload corroborates the same answers. Minor blemishes only: unused numeric fields render the literal string 'null', and the earlier observed duplicate/inconsistent Track display.
evidence_refs: obs: Noticed a possible display bug: the page shows 'Track: Agents' near the top summary but 'Track: Infra & Serving' further down

items.reasoning: Draft save and resume both work, implemented as autosave rather than an explicit button: after typing only the Title, a 'Draft saved [timestamp]' indicator appeared; after navigating away to the homepage and back to the form URL, the Welcome step read 'Resuming your saved draft' and the Title field was pre-filled with the exact text left behind. Screenshots were captured for both states and the transcript shows the navigate-away/return sequence (turns 9–13).
evidence_refs: obs: Draft auto-save is present: after typing only the Title, a "Draft saved [timestamp]" indicator appeared automatically
obs: Draft resume verified: ... 'Resuming your saved draft' and the Submission step had the Title field pre-filled

items.reasoning: The speaker appended 'Updated: now includes 2026 benchmark data.' to the description of SESS-10, received a 'Submission updated.' confirmation, and the sentence survived a direct-URL reload on the speaker side. The same sentence appears verbatim at the end of the Description on the organizer's submission detail page and in the API record for sub00000-...-010, confirming the edited content is what the organizer sees.
evidence_refs: obs: Persistence verified: reloaded submission detail page via direct URL navigation and the appended sentence 'Updated: now includes 2026 benchmark data.' is still present

items.reasoning: CFP-S3 ran out of turns before provisioning a reviewer or signing in as one. The only related evidence is the Evaluation screen, which shows review plans with per-plan reviewer checkbox lists (Frances Allen, Vint Cerf, James Ellis-Jones, Rosalind Franklin), a visibility selector ('all reviewers see all') and an 'Assign' button — i.e. reviewer assignment exists — but no reviewer was created/invited with usable credentials, and no reviewer-side dashboard was ever loaded, so role separation cannot be assessed. (Note: the admin 'Review' section itself errored with 'Failed to fetch' when the organizer opened it.)
evidence_refs: obs: Clicking 'Review' nav item threw a 'Failed to fetch' error on first load

items.reasoning: No review was ever recorded: CFP-S3 exhausted its turns before reaching a scorecard, and CFP-S4 confirmed via API that SESS-10 has review_count 0 and rating null. The submission detail page does contain a 'Reviews' section heading and the Evaluation screen tracks '12/18 reviews complete' per plan, so the data model exists, but the reviewer-side scoring flow, completion state and organizer-visible rating/comment were never exercised or observed.
evidence_refs: obs: the API confirms review_count:0 and rating:null for SESS-10

items.reasoning: The organizer never recorded an accept or reject decision. CFP-S4 spent its whole run blocked by a client-side defect: the Workspace Submissions/Speakers grids hang on 'Loading row…' forever (badge counts correct) and the DevFlow event shows 'Failed to load items: Failed to fetch', which the agent documented as blocking 'per-row status controls'. The app clearly models distinct decision statuses — the dashboard shows counters (6 Accepted, 6 Pending, 1 Declined, 2 Withdrawn) and rows badged pending/withdrawn/declined — but these are seeded values, and no decision control was located or used, so the organizer's ability to record decisions cannot be decided from this evidence.
evidence_refs: obs: CONFIRMED BUG ... The admin Workspace grid (Speakers and Submissions tabs) and the Review section fail to load data ... This blocks the organizer's primary UI path for opening a submission detail page, viewing per-submission reviews, using per-row status controls

items.reasoning: Status propagation to the submitter is demonstrably wired: the speaker portal's 'My Submissions' page shows per-submission status chips including 'Accepted' (SESS-1), 'Withdrawn' (SESS-4) and 'Pending', and the organizer side shows the same statuses (SESS-1 accepted, SESS-8 declined) — so organizer-side status values do surface in the speaker dashboard. However, the specific scenario was not completed: no accept/reject decision was recorded on 'Taming 40-Minute CI' or 'Your AI Pair Programmer...' (both remain Pending on both sides), so the end-to-end decision→speaker-dashboard round trip for the fixture proposals was never observed.

There are clear UI traces of a decision-notification capability but no observed dispatch. The admin submission detail header carries a per-submission notified indicator ('SESS-10 · Call for Speakers 2026 · Submitted Aug 7, 2026 · Not notified'), the dashboard surfaces '1 decision is staged but the speakers haven't been told yet', and the form builder has a dedicated step 6 'Notifications'. But no notify/send-decisions action was ever triggered, no template/compose step was seen, and no sent/queued confirmation or email log was captured, so the UI-observable half of the criterion is only partly evidenced.

An Agenda section exists in the admin navigation and the dashboard hints at handoff ('1 accepted session still needs a time slot on the agenda', plus an 'Agenda' tab), but CFP-S4 hit the turn limit before any acceptance was recorded or the agenda contents were inspected in an attached screenshot. No evidence shows whether an accepted submission's title/speaker/track carries over into the sessions/agenda area.

The close date was never moved into the past (CFP-S1 and CFP-S4 both ended at the turn limit before touching form settings), and no speaker-side attempt to edit a submission on a closed call was made. There is no evidence either way about post-close edit locking.

defects.description: The admin Workspace grids (Submissions and Speakers tabs) hang indefinitely on 'Loading row…' and never render rows even though the tab badges show correct counts (Submissions 15, Speakers 11); for the second event the grid shows 'Failed to load items: Failed to fetch' plus an 'Event switch failed: Failed to fetch' modal, and the 'Review' section errors with 'Failed to fetch'. The agent verified via direct API calls with the same session cookie that the backend returns full submission data, so this is a client-side defect. It blocks the organizer's primary path to submission details, per-row status/decision controls, and review data.
defects.where: Admin app: /app?v=workspace&...&tab=submissions | tab=speakers, and /app?v=review (both events)

defects.description: Conditional-field logic is inconsistent between the create form and the edit form: the edit-submission page always renders the Workshop-only fields ('Room Setup Requirements', 'Prerequisites') regardless of the selected format, and marks 'Room Setup Requirements' as required (*) even for a Talk-format submission — while the server does not enforce it (save succeeded with the field empty). Misleading required marker plus broken conditional visibility on edit.
defects.where: Speaker portal: edit submission page (/portal/ai-engineer-sandbox-event/submissions/<id> edit)

defects.description: Empty numeric fields render the literal string 'null' instead of a blank/em-dash after an edit ('Capacity: null', 'CEU Credits: null'), visible in both the speaker view and the organizer submission detail page.
defects.where: Submission detail (speaker portal and admin detail panel for SESS-10)

defects.description: The submission detail page displayed two different Track values for the same record in two places ('Track: Agents' in the top summary vs 'Track: Infra & Serving' in the field list), i.e. contradictory metadata shown to the user.
defects.where: Speaker portal submission detail for SESS-10 (pre-edit)

defects.description: A submission deep-link route (/app?v=submission&id=sub00000-...) appears to render the generic dashboard instead of the submission detail view, so direct links to a submission do not resolve to that record.
defects.where: Admin app: /app?v=submission&id=... (CFP-S4 screenshot 034)

areas.notes: Three of the four scenarios (CFP-S1, S3, S4) ended at the 70-turn limit, so the whole back half of the CFP lifecycle — close-date enforcement, reviewer provisioning/scoring, decision recording, notification dispatch, agenda handoff, post-close edit lock — was never exercised and is judged cannot_judge rather than absent. Much of the lost time in S3/S4 was caused by a real app defect (the admin workspace grid never loading), which is recorded as a critical defect but is not itself a rubric verdict. The speaker-side flow (CFP-S2) completed and is well evidenced: public wizard with deadline/tracks, autosave drafts with resume, required-field validation, conditional workshop fields, submission with confirmation code, status-labelled speaker dashboard, and edit persistence round-tripping to the organizer. Two persona adaptations affect strictness: the portal session was pre-authenticated as a fixed demo speaker (so account creation was untestable), and the seeded event is 'AI.Engineer Sandbox Event – NYC' rather than the DevFlow Conf 2027 fixture, so field names/tracks were mapped to nearest equivalents.

scenarios.scenarioName: Speaker drafts, submits, and edits proposals
scenarios.summary:
Executed the full CFP-S2 speaker draft/submit/edit scenario against KMS's real CFP flow (AI.Engineer Sandbox Event – NYC), adapting sample data to the app's actual seeded schema since the DevFlow Conf 2027 sample event does not exist in this app.

Key findings and evidence:
1. Public CFP portal: /submit/ai-engineer-sandbox-event/form0000-... — a 5-step wizard (Welcome → Account → Submission → Participant → Review). Already signed in as the fixed demo speaker identity 'Ada Lovelace' (ada@example.com), which stood in for Priya Raman since account/email fields are locked to the seeded persona.
2. Draft capability: confirmed via **autosave**, not a manual 'Save draft' button — typing the title alone triggered a 'Draft saved [timestamp]' indicator (screenshot captured). Navigated away to the homepage and back; the Welcome step showed 'Resuming your saved draft' and the title was pre-filled exactly as left (screenshot captured) — draft persistence verified.
3. Required-field validation: clicking Next with Description/Format/Tags/Track empty produced inline red alerts ('Description is required', 'Format is required', 'Tags is required', 'Track is required') — screenshot captured. Note: there is no separate 'abstract' vs 'Key takeaway' field in this event's schema; only a single 'Description' field ('What will attendees learn?') exists, so the key takeaway was appended within it as adaptation.
4. Conditional fields: selecting Format='Workshop' revealed 'Room Setup Requirements' and 'Prerequisites' fields (screenshot). Switching back to 'Talk' hid both again (screenshot) — confirms dynamic form logic works on the create form. (Noted a minor inconsistency: the Edit-submission page always shows these fields regardless of format, and marks 'Room Setup Requirements' as required even for a Talk-format submission — but the server did not enforce that on save.)
5. Completed and submitted 'Taming 40-Minute CI: Incremental Builds at Monorepo Scale' (Format=Talk, Track=Infra & Serving [closest equivalent to 'Platform & Infra'], Level=Intermediate, bio=Priya's fixture bio, key takeaway embedded in description). Filled-form screenshot taken before submit. Confirmation screen: 'Submission received — SESS-10' / 'Thanks for your proposal! Our track leads will review it and you will hear back by email.' — implies future email but does not explicitly state one was sent immediately.
6. Dashboard ('My Submissions' in the speaker portal) lists submissions with status labels (Pending/Accepted/Withdrawn) — verified SESS-10 listed as 'Pending'.
7. Edit test: opened SESS-10, appended 'Updated: now includes 2026 benchmark data.' to the Description, saved ('Submission updated.' confirmation), reloaded via direct URL navigation, and confirmed the sentence persisted server-side (screenshot).
8. Second full proposal ('Your AI Pair Programmer Is Lying to You...', Track=AI in Production [closest to 'AI Engineering'], Level=Advanced) — the public form initially blocked new submissions with 'You have reached the limit of 3 submissions for this form' (screenshot), a real product constraint since the seeded account already had 3 submissions. Withdrew one existing Pending submission (SESS-4) to free a slot, then successfully submitted the second proposal as SESS-15.
9. Final dashboard screenshot shows all 4 submissions with distinct status labels: SESS-15 (Pending), SESS-10 (Pending, with edited abstract), SESS-4 (Withdrawn), SESS-1 (Accepted, pre-seeded) — both target proposals from the scenario are present with status labels, satisfying the success signal.

Bugs/observations recorded: (a) inconsistent Track value shown in two places on submission detail page (top summary said 'Agents', detail list said 'Infra & Serving') for SESS-10 before edit; (b) 'Capacity'/'CEU Credits' render as literal string 'null' instead of blank/dash after an edit; (c) Edit-page always shows Workshop-only fields regardless of selected format, unlike the create-form's correct conditional hiding.
observations: Homepage is a demo chooser (KMS - AI.Engineer Sandbox Event NYC), not the DevFlow Conf 2027 sample data event. This is single-event seeded demo; no obvious multi-event creation UI visible on homepage yet. Task says browser already signed in as speaker persona - will verify by checking session state.

The public CFP form's Account step shows "Signed in as ada@example.com. Resuming your saved draft." This confirms the browser session is authenticated as the demo speaker persona (ada@example.com stands in for Priya Raman since account is pre-seeded/fixed identity), and there is already an existing saved draft from prior state (possibly seeded or from a previous CFP-S1 run).

Draft auto-save is present: after typing only the Title, a "Draft saved [timestamp]" indicator appeared automatically at the bottom of the Submission step — no manual 'Save draft' button needed, it autosaves. This satisfies the 'save as draft' capability requirement, implemented as autosave rather than an explicit button.

Required-field validation confirmed: clicking Next with Description/Format/Tags/Track empty shows inline alert messages ('Description is required', 'Format is required', 'Tags is required', 'Track is required'). This form uses 'Description' (What will attendees learn?) as the closest equivalent to abstract/key-takeaway; there is no separate 'Key takeaway' field in this event's CFP schema — noting as an adaptation since the seeded event differs from the sample DevFlow Conf 2027 schema.

Draft resume verified: after navigating away to homepage and back to the CFP form, the Welcome step showed 'Resuming your saved draft' and the Submission step had the Title field pre-filled with 'Taming 40-Minute CI: Incremental Builds at Monorepo Scale' exactly as left. Draft persistence works correctly.

Conditional field logic confirmed: selecting Format=Workshop reveals 'Room Setup Requirements' and 'Prerequisites' (What should attendees know or install beforehand?) fields. Switching Format back to 'Talk' hides both fields again. This is the app's equivalent of 'Workshop prerequisites' conditional visibility from the script.

The pre-authenticated speaker identity is fixed as 'Ada Lovelace' (ada@example.com) — email field is disabled/non-editable. This demo identity stands in for the sample data's Priya Raman. Filled the Biography field with Priya Raman's fixture bio text per instructions to use sample data content, while keeping the fixed name/email identity intact.

Confirmation screen exact wording: 'Submission received — SESS-10' with body 'Thanks for your proposal! Our track leads will review it and you will hear back by email.' followed by 'Taking you to your speaker portal in 3s…' and a 'Continue to portal' link. No explicit statement of a confirmation email being sent immediately, but text implies future email notification ('you will hear back by email').

Dashboard shows submission detail page for SESS-10 with status 'Pending'. Noticed a possible display bug: the page shows 'Track: Agents' near the top summary but 'Track: Infra & Serving' further down in the full definition list — inconsistent duplicate Track values for the same submission.

On the Edit submission page, 'Room Setup Requirements' and 'Prerequisites' fields are shown even though Format=Talk (not Workshop) — inconsistent with the create-form's conditional-visibility logic (which correctly hid these fields for Talk format). Possible minor bug in the edit view.

Edit save succeeded with confirmation 'Submission updated.' despite 'Room Setup Requirements' field being marked required (*) and left empty — server-side validation did not enforce that asterisk requirement for a Talk-format submission, confirming it's a UI labeling bug (field is only actually required for Workshop format).

Minor display bug: after editing/saving, 'Capacity' and 'CEU Credits' fields show the literal text 'null' instead of an empty dash '—' placeholder (as shown before the edit). Cosmetic backend/frontend null-handling issue.

Persistence verified: reloaded submission detail page via direct URL navigation and the appended sentence 'Updated: now includes 2026 benchmark data.' is still present in the Description, confirming the edit was saved server-side, not just client-state.

Attempting a second full proposal submission hit the seeded form's 'Submission limit: 3 per user' — the account (Ada Lovelace/ada@example.com) already had 3 submissions (SESS-1, SESS-4, and the new SESS-10) before this test even began. The form blocks further submissions with message: 'You have reached the limit of 3 submissions for this form. Manage your existing submissions in the speaker portal.' This is a real product constraint, not a bug — will proceed to withdraw the 'Accepted' SESS-1 is not advisable (would corrupt other test data); instead documenting this limit and using the existing submissions for the final dashboard screenshot with 2+ proposals already present.

observations: BUG: In the AI.Engineer Sandbox Event – NYC workspace, the Submissions and Speakers grids get stuck indefinitely on "Loading row…" and never render data (tab badges show correct counts e.g. Submissions 15, Speakers 11, but no rows appear). Clicking into the Review section for this event surfaced an explicit "Failed to fetch" error message. This happened consistently across multiple reloads/navigations.

CONFIRMED BUG (reproducible across fresh login, multiple events, multiple retries): The admin Workspace grid (Speakers and Submissions tabs) and the Review section fail to load data. Submissions/Speakers tabs show 'Loading row…' forever for the seeded 'AI.Engineer Sandbox Event – NYC', and show an explicit 'Failed to load items: Failed to fetch' error (plus a modal 'Event switch failed: Failed to fetch') for the 'DevFlow Conf 2027' event. The Review section shows 'Failed to fetch' outright. This blocks the organizer's primary UI path for opening a submission detail page, viewing per-submission reviews, using per-row status controls, and per-submission notified indicators. Verified via direct API calls (GET https://kms.r-s.workers.dev/api/v1/events/{id}/submissions and .../submissions/{id}) using the same browser session cookie that the underlying REST API itself works fine and returns full submission data (title, status, rating, review_count, answers, participants) - so this is a frontend/client-side defect in the workspace grid component, not a backend/data outage. Because the API confirms review_count:0 and rating:null for SESS-10 ('Taming 40-Minute CI: Incremental Builds at Monorepo Scale', speaker Ada Lovelace, not Priya Raman), no reviewer comment/rating of 4 from a 'Sam Whitfield' is present in this app's seeded data — the app's real seed is an unrelated 'AI.Engineer Sandbox Event' dataset, not the DevFlow Conf 2027 fixture data described in the scenario script. No matching submission with a rating-4 review was found among the visible seeded submissions (ratings seen: 1.83, 2.63, 3.25).

areas.title: Abstract Management (Review Depth & Disposition)

items.reasoning: All three scenarios ended in agent_error at the turn limit before the evaluation-plan configuration was reached. An 'Evaluation' section exists in the admin nav (visible in screenshots), and the agent navigated to ?v=evaluation twice, but the only captured screenshot of it shows an indefinite 'Loading…' state with no content, so nothing can be concluded about round configuration, names, dates, or per-round scorecards.
No evidence was gathered about reviewer pools at all; the agent never reached a reviewer-pool configuration screen. The Evaluation view it did open never rendered.
The scorecard editor was never opened and no reviewer scoring view was reached in any scenario. No screenshots of criteria types or a filled reviewer scorecard exist.

No weight configuration UI was observed and no controlled aggregate could be computed. The submissions grid does show numeric RATING values (e.g. ★1.83, ★4.63) for pre-seeded data, but there is no evidence about how they are computed or whether weights exist.
No assignment action was performed and no reviewer queue was ever loaded — the agent never signed in as a reviewer with an assigned queue before hitting the turn limit.

ABS-S2 spent its whole run trying to seed submissions into DevFlow Conf 2027 and never reached assignment tooling, so caps/auto-distribute/track-filtered bulk assignment were neither found nor ruled out.
evidence_refs: obs: DevFlow Conf 2027 event already exists ... it has 0 submissions

items.reasoning: Neither a per-round anonymization setting nor any reviewer-side view of a submission was observed. No basis to judge blinding.
No review progress dashboard was reached; the 'Review' section was clicked in ABS-S3 but no rendered screenshot of per-reviewer completion counts was captured before the turn limit.
No reminder/nudge control was located or exercised; the progress/reviewer view was never rendered in the evidence.

The organizer submissions grid does show a per-submission aggregate ('RATING' column with values like ★1.83, ★2.63, ★3.25, ★4.13, ★4.63) and it is sortable — the header reads 'RATING ↑' and the rows are ordered ascending by rating (unrated '—' rows first, then 1.83 → 4.63), which the agent labelled 'rating-sort-ascending'. However, the evidence does not show the descending toggle producing the reverse order, and no aggregate could be verified against reviews entered during this run (the intended 5.0 / ~3.0-3.33 submissions were never scored: 'Taming 40-Minute CI' shows '—'). So aggregation + one sort direction are demonstrated, but the correctness/round-trip of sorting and aggregate arithmetic is unverified.

Co-participants are supported at submission time: the CFP wizard's Participant step exposes 'Participant 2' with First/Last/Email and a per-participant Role dropdown, and the submission detail shows a Participants block with role labels ('Ada Lovelace · speaker · primary contact'). However the agent confirmed the Role dropdown offers only the single value 'speaker' — there is no distinct co-author/co-presenter role label — and no co-participant was actually persisted end-to-end (the confirmed SESS-16 shows only one participant), nor was the organizer-side review view of participants captured. Meaningful gaps: no differentiated co-author role and no retroactive add (submission edit exposes only Title/Description/Format).
evidence_refs: obs: KEY FINDING (co-author capability) ... Role dropdown only offers a single option, "speaker"

items.reasoning: The reviewer scoring view was never opened, so the presence or absence of a conflict-of-interest/recusal control could not be assessed.

The organizer submissions grid (which includes the STATUS and RATING/review-score columns) provides '↓ CSV' and '↓ XLSX' export controls at the bottom of the table, visible in multiple screenshots. However there is no evidence in the transcript that the agent clicked them, so no download initiation or success confirmation was observed, and no dedicated review-results/reports export was reached.

No AI-triage feature was seen or explicitly ruled out; the agent recorded no observation about AI review claims and never explored the Evaluation section's contents. Insufficient evidence to say the capability is absent.

defects.description: Admin workspace data grids frequently hang on 'Loading…' indefinitely or fail with 'Failed to load items: Failed to fetch' (Retry button), blocking organizer-side browsing of submissions and speakers. Reproduced across multiple scenarios and events.
defects.where: Admin: /app?v=workspace&tab=submissions and &tab=speakers (both DevFlow Conf 2027 and AI.Engineer Sandbox Event)

defects.description: The Evaluation section rendered only 'Loading…' with no content on repeated visits, so evaluation/round configuration was unreachable.

Submitting the public CFP form while authenticated as an organizer account fails at Submit with an on-screen 'participants_invalid' error even though the Participant step shows a valid primary contact; a partial submission record is nonetheless persisted (workspace count 0→1) and stays stuck in a draft/invalid state, producing orphaned data.
defects.where: Public CFP: /submit/devflow-conf-2027/0ba2e574-... final Submit step

defects.description: Co-participants can only be added during the initial submission wizard; neither the submission detail page nor the 'Edit submission' form exposes any participant add/edit control, so a co-presenter can never be added to an existing submission.
defects.where: Speaker portal: /portal/.../submissions/<id> and /edit

defects.description: The participant Role dropdown offers only a single value ('speaker'), so there is no way to label a co-author/co-presenter distinctly.
defects.where: CFP wizard step 4 'Participant'

defects.description: Clicking a nav item sometimes lands on a different tab than the one clicked (e.g. clicking Submissions results in the Speakers tab being active), indicating unreliable tab/route state handling.
defects.where: Admin left nav / workspace tabs (turns 24-28 ABS-S1, turns 14-19 ABS-S2)

areas.notes: All three scenarios terminated at the 70-turn limit (agent_error) without reaching the core review-workflow features. ABS-S1 was derailed by a fixed single demo speaker identity (Ada Lovelace only, no signup for Priya Raman) plus a 3-submissions-per-user cap; ABS-S2 discovered the fixture submissions did not exist under DevFlow Conf 2027 and burned its turns trying to seed them, hitting a 'participants_invalid' submit bug; ABS-S3 spent its turns fighting perpetual 'Loading…' grids and event-switching. Consequently ABS-01 through ABS-09, ABS-12 and ABS-14 have essentially no evidence and are cannot_judge rather than not_found — the app clearly has 'Evaluation' and 'Review' sections in its admin nav that were never successfully rendered. Only two items could be partly judged from the submissions grid (aggregate RATING column with an ascending sort, CSV/XLSX export controls) and the co-participant capability observed in the CFP wizard.

scenarios.scenarioName: Speaker seeds submissions with a co-author
scenarios.summary: Turn limit (70) reached before the scenario finished.
observations: App identity mismatch: The site is seeded as "AI.Engineer Sandbox Event – NYC" (not "DevFlow Conf 2027") with a fixed demo speaker identity "Ada Lovelace" (ada@example.com) — there is no signup flow to become "Priya Raman" specifically; the "Demo speaker login" button always logs in as Ada Lovelace via a magic-link. Proceeding using Ada Lovelace as the stand-in for the speaker persona since submission titles from the fixture already exist under this account (evidence of a prior chained run). This is a real product constraint: single fixed demo speaker account, not multi-identity signup.

Public CFP form (form0000-...-000000000001) enforces "Submission limit: 3 per user". Ada Lovelace already has 3 counted submissions (SESS-15 AI Pair Programmer - Pending, SESS-10 Taming 40-Minute CI - Pending, SESS-1 Building Reliable Multi-Agent Pipelines - Accepted; SESS-4 is Withdrawn and apparently doesn't count against the limit, or does). The form now shows "You have reached the limit of 3 submissions for this form" with only a Back button — no override. This will block submitting the 3rd fixture proposal ("Docs That Answer Back") as this speaker identity via the public form.

BUG: Admin Workspace > Submissions tab gets stuck showing "Loading…" indefinitely and never renders rows, even after multiple waits/re-clicks. This blocks organizer-side submission list browsing via this route.
Confirmed transient error: Admin Submissions grid shows "Failed to load items: Failed to fetch" with a Retry button. This is a real bug/flakiness in the admin workspace data grid for this event.

KEY FINDING (co-author capability): The app DOES have an "Add participant" control with per-participant Role dropdown, but it is only exposed during the initial multi-step submission wizard (step 4 "Participant") for a NEW submission — confirmed on form0000...000000000002 ("Submit a Session"). The Role dropdown only offers a single option, "speaker" (attempted to select "co-speaker" and it did not exist — confirmed by inspecting dropdown, which showed only "speaker"). So there is no distinct "Co-author/Co-presenter" role label, just repeated "speaker" entries. Critically, once a submission exists, NEITHER the submission detail page NOR its "Edit submission" page (checked for SESS-10 "Taming 40-Minute CI" and for the freshly-created SESS-16) expose any participant-add control — the edit form only lets you change Title/Description/Format/etc. This means a co-author CANNOT be added to an already-submitted proposal like "Taming 40-Minute CI" through the speaker portal; the only entry point for adding a co-presenter is during the original submission flow, before first submit. Since SESS-10 was already submitted (from a prior seed/run) with only Ada Lovelace as participant, there is no in-product way, as this speaker, to retroactively add Marcus Okafor to it.

areas.title: Speaker Management

items.reasoning: A dedicated Speakers roster exists under Workspace with columns FIRST NAME / LAST NAME / EMAIL / COMPANY / JOB TITLE and a search box: typing 'sbek-speaker' narrows the list to a single matching row (Speakers count drops to 1) and clearing it restores the two-row list, so the search/restore half is clearly demonstrated. The gap is identity content: the only rows visible in the DevFlow roster are an email-only record with blank first/last name, company and job title, and the organizer's own account — no evidence was captured of a roster row rendering a speaker's name together with title/company, because the manual add in SPK-S1 was blocked by duplicate-email validation and the run hit the turn limit before a populated roster was screenshotted.
evidence_refs: obs: Duplicate email validation works correctly... A blank speaker record with Priya's fixture email already existed

items.reasoning: The manual add-speaker form exists and accepts the required profile fields — the agent filled First name, Last name, Email, Company, Job title and Biography (observed field set also includes mobile phone, pronouns, internal notes). However the create submission returned 'A contact with this email already exists for this event.' so no saved record displaying those values was ever shown, and the SBEK-ORG-EDIT-01 organizer bio edit plus reload check was never performed (turn limit reached). Persistence of organizer-side edits is therefore unverified.
evidence_refs: obs: Speaker add form fields: First name, Last name, Email, Company, Job title, Mobile phone, Pronouns, Biography, Internal notes
obs: Duplicate email validation works correctly: 'A contact with this email already exists for this event.'

items.reasoning: The agent never reached a CSV import attempt — SPK-S1 hit the turn limit while still trying to open a speaker record, and no observation records searching for or failing to find an import control. The roster footer shows '↓ CSV' and '↓ XLSX' buttons, but those are exports, not imports, so absence of an import capability cannot be concluded either. Dana Kowalski never appears in any captured roster.
evidence_refs: obs: Turn limit (70) reached before the scenario finished (SPK-S1 summary)

items.reasoning: No status control was exercised. The organizer dashboard's Speaker Tracking tab does display a confirmation vocabulary ('Confirmed 3 / Awaiting confirmation 2'), implying a workflow status field exists, but no evidence shows a control changing a speaker's status, persistence across reload, or a status filter on the roster. The agent was cut off before reaching a speaker record detail panel.
evidence_refs: obs: Turn limit (70) reached before the scenario finished (SPK-S1 summary)

items.reasoning: Task creation was never attempted: SPK-S1 exhausted its turns on the roster, and the three fixture general tasks were never created (the agent noted 0 tasks exist for DevFlow Conf 2027). There is circumstantial evidence of an organizer task model — a workspace Tasks tab and a task table with TASK / ASSIGNEE / FOR / STATUS / DUE / COMPLETED columns, plus a dashboard overdue-tasks table listing task, speaker and due date — but no creation form with title, due date and multi-speaker assignment was observed.
evidence_refs: obs: ...There is no Marcus Okafor speaker, 0 tasks exist for the event

items.reasoning: No invite/welcome-email control was located or triggered. The dashboard exposes 'Send reminder' and 'Remind all (1)' controls for overdue tasks (deliverables-reminder territory, owned elsewhere) and the workspace has a Messages tab with non-zero counts, but the agent never opened a per-speaker invite or portal-access control, so neither presence nor absence of a portal invitation flow can be decided. Portal access in this app is via a magic link surfaced on the demo login page.

A distinct speaker portal exists at /portal/ai-engineer-sandbox-event with its own Home / Submissions / Profile / Tasks navigation and a header identifying the signed-in speaker ('Ada Lovelace' with avatar and Logout), clearly separate from the KMS admin workspace. The portal shows only that speaker's submissions, profile and tasks; the agent explicitly checked the submission detail, profile and task pages and recorded that no other speaker's name appeared anywhere. Access was via a per-speaker magic link the agent could exercise. The identity is the demo's seeded speaker (Ada) rather than the fixture's Priya, which reflects the fixed demo seeding, not a scoping failure.
evidence_refs: obs: Session SESS-10 page shows only participant 'Ada Lovelace' — no other speaker names appear
obs: Scoping: ... only Ada Lovelace's own data appeared; no Marcus Okafor or Dana Kowalski name appeared anywhere in the portal

items.reasoning: The portal half is well evidenced: the profile form offers Biography, Headshot upload and LinkedIn/Twitter/Facebook/Website URL fields; the agent saved the sentinel bio 'SBEK-PORTAL-BIO-01', LinkedIn and Twitter URLs (URL validation caught the bare @handle) and uploaded headshot.png, which rendered as the profile image, and a full reload of /profile confirmed all three persisted. The organizer-side confirmation is only indirect: the dashboard's Asset Completeness panel lists Ada as missing only 'slides' (i.e. bio and headshot are registered organizer-side), but no organizer view of her record showing the same sentinel bio text and headshot was captured before the SPK-S3 run hit its turn limit.

Priya's stand-in portal shows three assigned tasks each with a due date and a status badge (Speaker Agreement, Due Aug 5 2026; Speaker Profile & Headshot, Due Sep 12 2026; Presentation Upload, Due Sep 28 2026), all initially 'not started'. The agent completed the first two via checkbox + Confirm, each producing a 'Task completed — thank you!' confirmation and flipping to a green 'complete' badge with a completion date; the reloaded task list (no flash banner present) still shows two complete and Presentation Upload 'not started', so the state persisted and the untouched task remained incomplete.

The organizer-side file listing was never reached: SPK-S3 spent its turns failing to open Ada's speaker record and hit the turn limit. The only organizer-side signal about the uploaded headshot is the dashboard's Asset Completeness panel implying a headshot exists for Ada; no filename, uploader/timestamp metadata, or download/view control was observed, and no evidence shows such a listing is absent.
evidence_refs: obs: Turn limit (70) reached before the scenario finished (SPK-S3 summary)

items.reasoning: The portal half is confirmed: the speaker's Submissions area lists SESS-10 'Taming 40-Minute CI: Incremental Builds at Monorepo Scale' with an exact fixture title match, and its detail page shows her as the participant. The organizer-side half is unverified — the agent never succeeded in opening the speaker's admin record or a session detail showing the speaker link before the SPK-S3 turn limit, so the organizer-visible speaker↔session link was not evidenced.
evidence_refs: obs: Session SESS-10 page shows only participant 'Ada Lovelace'
obs: Turn limit (70) reached before the scenario finished (SPK-S3 summary)

items.reasoning: A list-level progress view exists: the dashboard's 'Speaker Tracking' tab shows Accepted Speakers, Outstanding Speaker Tasks, a Confirmed/Awaiting confirmation donut, 'Top speakers by outstanding tasks' (Grace Hopper 2 (1 overdue), Ada Lovelace 1), per-speaker Asset Completeness chips, and an overdue-tasks table with task, speaker, due date and overdue days — and it reflects the portal completions (Ada's count dropped to the single remaining Presentation Upload after she completed two tasks). The gap: this is an aggregate/outstanding-count view rather than a per-speaker × per-task completion matrix, and the workspace task table that would show that (TASK/ASSIGNEE/STATUS/DUE/COMPLETED columns) was stuck on 'Loading...' in every capture, so which specific tasks each speaker completed was not observable, and no complete/incomplete filter was demonstrated.

No bulk-compose flow was opened. A 'Messages' tab exists in the workspace with non-zero counts (1 for DevFlow, 2 for AI.Engineer), suggesting a communications area with logged messages, but recipient selection, the compose form with the fixture subject, a send success state and a history entry were never exercised — SPK-S3 ran out of turns while still on the speakers list.
evidence_refs: obs: Turn limit (70) reached before the scenario finished (SPK-S3 summary)

items.reasoning: Email templates and merge-field personalization were never reached; the agent never opened the Messages/compose area, so there is no evidence of template bodies with tokens or of a resolved per-recipient preview, and equally no evidence that templates are absent.
evidence_refs: obs: Turn limit (70) reached before the scenario finished (SPK-S3 summary)

items.reasoning: The agent enumerated the speaker record's field set on the create form and recorded it as First name, Last name, Email, Company, Job title, Mobile phone, Pronouns, Biography, Internal notes — no travel/logistics or custom field. The portal profile likewise offers only name, pronouns, company, job title, bio, headshot and social URLs. The Settings page contains only API tokens, API docs and a demo-data reset, with no custom-field configuration. No travel-preference or generic custom field capable of holding the logistics text was found (the free-text 'Internal notes' field is an organizer note, not a dedicated logistics field, and was not exercised).
evidence_refs: obs: Speaker add form fields: First name, Last name, Email, Company, Job title, Mobile phone, Pronouns, Biography, Internal notes. No Twitter/LinkedIn/dietary/t-shirt fields exist
obs: Profile page: ... there is a Pronouns dropdown, Company, Job title, Headshot upload, and LinkedIn/Twitter/Facebook/Website URL fields

areas.notes: Two of the three scenarios (SPK-S1 roster/tasks and SPK-S3 progress/comms) ended at the 70-turn limit, largely because the agent could not open a speaker record detail panel (repeated clicks, Tab/Enter and URL-based ?rec= navigation attempts did not visibly open an editable record in the captured screenshots). That leaves the organizer-side half of this area largely unevidenced: CSV import, status changes/filters, task creation, invitations, bulk email, templates and the organizer file listing were never exercised, so those items are cannot_judge rather than not_found. The app is also a single fixed demo instance seeded around 'AI.Engineer Sandbox Event – NYC' with a shared speaker account (Ada Lovelace) rather than the fixture identities (Priya/Marcus/Dana); the agent substituted Ada as the speaker persona, which is a harness/seeding mismatch and not itself an application defect. The speaker portal half of the area (scoped portal, profile editing with sentinel bio + headshot + social links, task list with due dates and persistent completion) was exercised end-to-end and works well.

scenarios.scenarioName: Speaker completes onboarding in the portal
scenarios.summary:
Completed SPK-S2 speaker onboarding walkthrough against the app's actual seeded data. Key finding: the app is a single fixed-demo instance ('AI.Engineer Sandbox Event – NYC') with no Priya Raman/Marcus Okafor/Dana Kowalski accounts — the demo speaker persona is 'Ada Lovelace' (ada@example.com, demo magic-link login from the root page), which stood in for Priya. Notably Ada's profile bio was already pre-populated with Priya's exact fixture bio text from an earlier scenario, indicating a single shared speaker account rather than per-scenario isolated identities.

Verified: (1) Portal dashboard (/portal/ai-engineer-sandbox-event) clearly identifies Ada Lovelace via avatar/name in a dedicated speaker-facing nav (Home/Submissions/Profile/Tasks), distinct from organizer admin. (2) Scoping check: no other speaker's name (Marcus Okafor, Dana Kowalski) appeared anywhere in submissions, profile, or tasks — only Ada's own data was visible. (3) Session 'Taming 40-Minute CI: Incremental Builds at Monorepo Scale' (SESS-10) was found under My Submissions with exact title match; no room/time shown since status is 'Pending' (not yet scheduled). (4) Profile editing: added sentinel bio text 'SBEK-PORTAL-BIO-01', filled LinkedIn and Twitter/X URLs (Twitter required full URL, not @handle — validation worked correctly), uploaded headshot.png which rendered as an avatar image; all changes persisted after a full page reload. (5) Task list showed 3 tasks with due dates and status badges (Speaker Agreement, Speaker Profile & Headshot, Presentation Upload) — task names differ from the fixture's 5-task list but map conceptually (Speaker Agreement≈Confirm participation, Speaker Profile & Headshot≈Complete bio/profile, Presentation Upload left incomplete≈Sign release form). areas.title: Content Management & Speaker Deliverables

items.reasoning: The S1 organizer scenario hit the 70-turn limit while still creating speakers and submitting CFP entries (turns 1-32); it never opened a task-creation form or created the two fixture file-request tasks. The admin sidebar does expose a Workspace > Tasks section (image 1, image 13) and seeded speaker-facing tasks carry instructions and due dates (image 10), but no evidence shows an organizer creating a file-request task with instructions, due date and assignee. Insufficient evidence to decide.
evidence_refs: turn 30 (CNT-S1) still on CFP submission form

items.reasoning: The speaker portal has a Tasks page listing assigned tasks with due dates and status badges (Presentation Upload — Due Sep 28 2026, tied to SESS-1; Speaker Agreement; Speaker Profile & Headshot), and the slides.pdf upload succeeded: clicking 'Upload & complete' produced a 'Task completed — thank you!' banner and the task flipped to 'complete' with 'Completed Aug 9, 2026'. Meaningful gap: no filename, attachment record, or download/view link for slides.pdf appears anywhere afterwards (Tasks page, Home, Submissions list, submission detail, submission edit all checked), so the file is not visibly recorded against the task or session — only a completion flag. Also, the headshot task in this build is a combined 'Speaker Profile & Headshot' task already complete in seed data.
evidence_refs: obs: After completing the 'Presentation Upload' task ... no filename, no download/view link ...

items.reasoning: Scope isolation is well evidenced: signed in as the speaker, Home/Submissions/Profile/Tasks show only that speaker's own 5 submissions and 3 tasks, with no trace of any other speaker (obs, portal-scope screenshot; final tasks screenshot shows only the speaker's own tasks). Admin-route probing returned plain 404s. However, the probed paths (/admin, /organizer, /dashboard/..., /workspace/..., /events/...) do not exist for any role in this app — the real organizer surface is /app, which the agent's recorded probe list does not include — so the 404s do not actually demonstrate that the organizer app is denied to a speaker session. Isolation half proven, admin-block half unproven.
evidence_refs: obs: Final state ... the speaker portal ... shows ONLY Ada Lovelace's/Priya's own 5 submissions and tasks; no trace of Marcus Okafor

items.reasoning: The agent searched the Tasks page, Home, Submissions list, submission detail and submission edit page after the upload and found no version list, no 'latest' flag, and no re-upload/replace control once the task was completed — the upload is a one-shot 'Upload & complete' action. Versioning capability appears absent from the speaker surface; no version UI was observable anywhere reachable.
evidence_refs: obs: ... (2) no version list / v1 vs v2 comparison, (3) no way to upload a second version once the task is marked complete
obs: Confirmed no re-upload control exists for a completed task in this UI

items.reasoning: No comment box or file-level thread exists anywhere in the speaker portal after upload (Tasks, Home, Submissions list, submission detail SESS-1, submission edit all checked). The speaker half of the required cross-role thread therefore cannot exist. The organizer side was never reached (S3 turn-limited), but with no comment affordance on the file at all on the speaker side, the criterion as written cannot be satisfied.
evidence_refs: obs: ... no comment box ... This means: (1) no way to add a comment on the uploaded file

items.reasoning: The upload control on the speaker task explicitly states the constraint 'File (PDF, PowerPoint — max 20 MB)', i.e. both accepted types and a maximum size, at the point of upload. This was recorded as a direct observation of the pre-upload task UI (screenshot 005 taken at that step, not attached, but the observation is explicit and consistent with the successful PDF upload that followed).
evidence_refs: obs: File constraint shown: 'File (PDF, PowerPoint — max 20 MB)'
turn 7-9 (CNT-S2) tasks-before-upload screenshot then slides.pdf upload

items.reasoning: Both organizer scenarios ended on the turn limit before the deliverables/tracking dashboard was captured. There are hints of tracking (dashboard chips '1 speaker has outstanding tasks', '1 speaker task is overdue', a 'Speaker Tracking' dashboard tab, and a Workspace > Tasks tab that accepted a search query producing ?q= filtering at turns 18-21 of S3), but no attached screenshot shows per-speaker per-task rows, due dates, statuses, or a filter visibly changing the set. Insufficient evidence.
evidence_refs: turn 18-21 (CNT-S3) filled tasks search with 'Lovelace' then 'SESS-1'

items.reasoning: The S3 organizer run was turn-limited before any reminder action was attempted. A Messages section exists in the admin nav, but no evidence shows a bulk reminder targeted at outstanding deliverable tasks or a send confirmation.

The agent opened a submission detail view in S3 (turns 24-27) but the run ended at the turn limit before any title/abstract edit was made, saved, or re-verified after reload. No attached screenshot shows an edit form, an updated title, or a persisted change.

No bio/headshot edit was performed or verified. The admin does provide a speaker record form including a Biography field (New Speaker form captured in S1), and the speaker portal has a Profile page with a headshot section, but persistence of an organizer-side bio edit and a newly uploaded headshot.png was never demonstrated because both organizer scenarios were turn-limited.
No content edit was made, so no change-history panel or restore action was ever exercised or observed. The S3 run stopped at the turn limit well before this step.

The submissions grid exposes a per-row Status dropdown and status filter chips (All/Pending/Accept Queue/Accepted/... /Draft), but that is the acceptance-decision status; no content approval/review state was set and no public agenda or preview surface was opened, so the gating behaviour is unverified. The S3 run was turn-limited before this step and the agent recorded no deferral observation.

The admin navigation is fully visible in several screenshots (Dashboard, Workspace > Speakers/Submissions/Tasks/Messages, Forms, Evaluation, Review, Agenda, Settings) and contains no files/assets library. On the speaker side the agent confirmed the uploaded slides.pdf is not surfaced with any filename, date or version metadata anywhere. No aggregate files view was found, though the organizer submission detail was not exhaustively inspected for a per-session Files tab before the turn limit.
evidence_refs: obs: ... no filename, no download/view link ... appear anywhere

items.reasoning: Row checkboxes for multi-select and CSV/XLSX export buttons are visible on the submissions grid, but those are tabular data exports, not a bulk file/ZIP download of latest versions, and the agent never attempted a bulk file export before the S3 turn limit. No evidence of an export dialog, grouping options, or a generation/ready confirmation either way.

defects.description: An uploaded deliverable disappears from the UI: after 'Upload & complete', slides.pdf is nowhere visible — no filename, no download/preview link, no attachment record on the task, session, or profile. From the user's perspective the file is unrecoverable and unverifiable by either role.
defects.where: Speaker portal /portal/ai-engineer-sandbox-event/tasks and submission detail/edit pages

defects.description: Upload is a one-shot irreversible action: once a file-request task is completed there is no replace/re-upload control, so a speaker who uploads the wrong file has no in-product remedy and no versioning exists.
defects.where: Speaker portal Tasks page (completed 'Presentation Upload' task)

defects.description: Admin list views frequently remain stuck on 'Loading...' — the Review view, Forms list, and the Speakers/Submissions grids show a persistent 'Loading…' placeholder in multiple captures, forcing repeated waits and re-navigation.
defects.where: KMS Admin /app?v=review, /app?v=forms, /app?v=workspace list grids

defects.description: A speaker record exists with empty first and last name (only an email address), producing a blank row in the speakers grid.
defects.where: KMS Admin > Workspace > Speakers (DevFlow Conf 2027)

areas.notes: Evidence quality is very uneven: only CNT-S2 (speaker side) completed; both organizer scenarios (CNT-S1 setup, CNT-S3 tracking/editing/approval/export) hit the 70-turn limit early, S1 having spent its budget creating speakers and CFP submissions and S3 browsing lists that were slow to load. Consequently the entire organizer half of this area (deliverables dashboard, reminders, content editing, change history, approval gate, files library, ZIP export) is largely unverified rather than demonstrated absent — hence many cannot_judge verdicts. Fixture identities also differ from the script: the app is seeded with a fixed demo speaker 'Ada Lovelace' (bearing Priya Raman's bio) and a combined 'Speaker Profile & Headshot' task already marked complete, so the before/after contrast the script expected could not be produced. What is solidly established: the speaker portal task list with due dates/status, a working single-file upload with an explicit type/size constraint, correct per-speaker data scoping, and the clear absence of file versioning and file-level commenting on the speaker side.

scenarios.summary: Turn limit (70) reached before the scenario finished.

scenarios.scenarioName: Speaker uploads and versions a deliverable
scenarios.summary:
Executed the CNT-S2 speaker deliverable-versioning scenario end-to-end against https://kms.r-s.workers.dev, adapting to the app's actual seed data.

AUTH: Root page was in a logged-out state (contrary to AUTH note). Used the app's own 'Demo speaker login' door, which triggers a visible magic-link (email not required, link shown directly in UI) and signs in as the seeded demo speaker 'Ada Lovelace' (ada@example.com). Notably, this account's Profile fields (bio, LinkedIn, Twitter) are pre-filled with Priya Raman's exact fixture bio/links, confirming it's the intended stand-in identity for this test persona. Documented this substitution explicitly.

PORTAL & TASKS (steps 2-3): Speaker portal has Home/Submissions/Profile/Tasks nav. Before upload, Tasks page showed 'Presentation Upload (required)' — Due Sep 28, 2026, status 'not started', tied to SESS-1 'Building Reliable Multi-Agent Pipelines with Tool-Use Guardrails' (the seed's actual accepted talk; a pending submission SESS-10 'Taming 40-Minute CI' also exists but has no linked upload task — noted as a data mismatch, not a missing feature). Two other tasks, 'Speaker Agreement' and 'Speaker Profile & Headshot' (the closest analog to 'Upload Final Headshot'), were ALREADY marked complete in the seed data before this test started — so the script's expectation of an incomplete headshot task could not be verified as a before/after; documented as a finding. File constraint shown in the upload UI: 'File (PDF, PowerPoint — max 20 MB)'. Screenshotted.

UPLOAD (step 4): Uploaded slides.pdf via the task's file input and clicked 'Upload & complete'. Task immediately flipped to status 'complete' with a banner 'Task completed — thank you!' and a 'Completed Aug 9, 2026' line. Screenshotted.

MAJOR GAP FOUND (steps 5-6): After completion, there is NO visible filename/attachment record, NO download/view link, NO comment box, and NO way to re-upload or replace the file (checked Tasks page, Home, Submissions list, Submission detail for SESS-1, and Submission edit page — none show any file/attachment UI). This means the scenario's requirements for (a) adding an author-attributed timestamped comment on the uploaded file, and (b) uploading a second version and viewing a version list with v1/v2 and 'latest' flagged, COULD NOT BE PERFORMED — no such UI surface exists for speakers in this app. This is recorded as an explicit missing-capability finding, not papered over.

MARK-COMPLETE (step 7): No separate explicit 'mark complete' action exists; upload and completion are a single atomic action ('Upload & complete'). Headshot task could not be 'left incomplete' as it was already complete in seed data.

SCOPING CHECK (step 8): Browsed Home/Submissions/Profile/Tasks — the entire portal is scoped strictly to the signed-in speaker's own 5 submissions and 3 tasks; no trace of Marcus Okafor or any other speaker anywhere. Screenshotted. Then probed admin/organizer routes while still authenticated as the speaker: /admin, /admin/ai-engineer-sandbox-event, /organizer, /dashboard/ai-engineer-sandbox-event, /workspace/ai-engineer-sandbox-event, and /events/ai-engineer-sandbox-event/submissions all returned a plain '404 Not Found' page (no data leakage, no crash), while the speaker's own /portal/* session remained valid throughout — confirmed via re-navigation. Screenshotted a representative 404. This demonstrates admin functionality is not reachable/exposed to the speaker account, though the app returns generic 404s rather than an explicit 403/'access denied' message.

FINAL STATE (step 9): Screenshotted final Tasks page: Presentation Upload = complete; Speaker Agreement = complete; Speaker Profile & Headshot = complete (was already complete pre-test, not exercised as an 'incomplete' contrast case as scripted).

Overall: core single-file upload-to-task-completion flow works and is scoped correctly per-speaker with no visible cross-speaker leakage or admin access, but the product has NO deliverable versioning (no v1/v2 history, no 'latest' flag) and NO file-level commenting feature anywhere reachable from the speaker portal — both explicit success signals from the scenario are unmet due to absent functionality, not user error.
observations: Root page shows a logged-out state with 'Demo admin login' and 'Demo speaker login' buttons, contrary to the AUTH note claiming an already-signed-in session. The seeded demo speaker is 'ada@example.com', not Priya Raman. Proceeding with Demo speaker login to reach the speaker portal, noting the identity mismatch.

Signed in via demo speaker magic-link as 'Ada Lovelace' (ada@example.com), standing in for the Priya Raman fixture identity since the app is pre-seeded with a fixed demo speaker account. Submissions include the exact titles from the sample data (e.g. SESS-10 'Taming 40-Minute CI'), confirming this is the same seeded dataset. Proceeding with Ada as the speaker persona.

Task list differs from script expectations: there is only ONE presentation-upload task, tied to SESS-1 'Building Reliable Multi-Agent Pipelines with Tool-Use Guardrails' (not 'Taming 40-Minute CI' as the scenario names, though that submission does exist as SESS-10 pending). There is no separate 'Upload Final Headshot' task; instead a combined 'Speaker Profile & Headshot' task exists and is already marked 'complete' (completed Aug 9, 2026), so it cannot be left incomplete as scripted — it was already done in seed data. File constraint shown: 'File (PDF, PowerPoint — max 20 MB)'. Proceeding with the actual seeded task (Presentation Upload for SESS-1) as the functional equivalent.

After completing the 'Presentation Upload' task, the tasks page shows only status 'complete' and 'Completed Aug 9, 2026' — no filename, no download/view link, no comment box, and no re-upload/replace control appear anywhere (checked Tasks page, Submissions list, Submission detail SESS-1, and Submission edit page). This means: (1) no way to add a comment on the uploaded file, (2) no version list / v1 vs v2 comparison, (3) no way to upload a second version once the task is marked complete via this UI. This is a significant capability gap vs the scenario's expected deliverable-versioning + commenting feature.

Confirmed no re-upload control exists for a completed task in this UI - the 'Presentation Upload' task shows only static 'complete' status with completion date, no button to add another version. This blocks steps 5-6 of the script (comment on file, second version upload) as no such UI surface exists for speakers.

Final state: 'Presentation Upload' task shows complete (slides.pdf uploaded successfully, task auto-completed on upload). 'Speaker Agreement' and 'Speaker Profile & Headshot' tasks were already complete in seed data before this test began, so the scripted requirement to 'leave headshot incomplete' could not be demonstrated as a distinct before/after — it was already complete going in. Scoping check: the speaker portal (Home, Submissions, Profile, Tasks) shows ONLY Ada Lovelace's/Priya's own 5 submissions and tasks; no trace of Marcus Okafor or any other speaker's name/session anywhere in the UI. Admin route probing while authenticated as speaker: /admin, /admin/ai-engineer-sandbox-event, /organizer, /dashboard/ai-engineer-sandbox-event, /workspace/ai-engineer-sandbox-event, /events/ai-engineer-sandbox-event/submissions all returned a plain 404 Not Found (not a login redirect or 403), while the speaker session itself remained valid on /portal/* routes throughout. This indicates route-level isolation (organizer app is on a separate path/subdomain not guessable, or requires distinct auth) rather than a visible 403/permission-denied UI, but no admin data was ever exposed to the speaker account.

areas.title: AI Agenda & Schedule Builder

items.reasoning: The agenda builder exists with List/Day/Week/Month/Rooms/Conflicts views, a day switcher (Tue, May 11 dropdown with prev/next arrows), a time axis (6 AM–5 PM in Day view), an Unscheduled pool, and a Rooms grid with room rows × day columns. The seeded event screenshot shows session cards positioned within room rows across three day columns (Mon Oct 12 / Tue Oct 13 / Wed Oct 14). Gap: for the fixture DevFlow event the room/track dimension is empty (no rooms exist), and the day labels are off by one from the configured event dates (May 11–13 shown vs May 12–14 configured), so the structure is present but partially incorrect for the target event.
evidence_refs: obs: Agenda builder day columns show Tue, May 11 / Wed, May 12 / Thu, May 13 even though the event dates are configured as May 12–14, 2027

items.reasoning: The agent searched the agenda builder (all view modes and the Add Session dialog's Room/Track dropdowns), Settings, Forms admin, the new-event dialog, and the REST API docs, and found no organizer-facing UI to create rooms or tracks. For the fresh DevFlow Conf 2027 event, the Room dropdown offered only 'No room' and Track only 'No track', while the pre-seeded AI.Engineer event has 6 rooms and 5 tracks — confirming rooms/tracks are seed-only fixtures. Selecting a room value in the Add Session dialog failed because the option did not exist.
evidence_refs: obs: FINDING: No UI for creating/configuring agenda Rooms or Tracks was found anywhere in the app
obs: In the Agenda 'Add session' dialog for DevFlow Conf 2027, the Track dropdown only offers 'No track' and the Room dropdown only offers 'No room'

items.reasoning: The 'Taming 40-Minute CI' session was created and appears in the agenda (List view shows SESS-2 with 'Unscheduled' in the When column, and it appears in the Unscheduled pool of the Day view), but it was never placed into a Day 1 10:00 / Room 2A slot: no rooms exist for this event so no room could be selected, and the agent hit the turn limit before performing/verifying a placement plus reload. Placement into a room slot is not achievable for this event because Room offers only 'No room'. Evidence of a successful timed+room placement and reload persistence is absent; the session remained unscheduled in every captured state.
evidence_refs: obs: Room dropdown only offers 'No room'

items.reasoning: Both scenarios ended in agent_error at the turn limit before two overlapping Priya Raman sessions were scheduled, so no conflict-trigger attempt was made. A 'Conflicts' tab exists in the agenda builder (showing a badge of 1 on the seeded event), which hints at conflict detection, but there is no evidence of a speaker double-booking warning being produced for the fixture scenario.
evidence_refs: agent summary: Turn limit (70) reached before the scenario finished

items.reasoning: Step 9 (second session in the same room at the same time) was never reached — the agent ran out of turns and, moreover, no rooms exist for the fixture event so room-overlap could not be exercised. No evidence of blocked placement or a room-conflict warning either way.
evidence_refs: agent summary: Turn limit (70) reached before the scenario finished
obs: Room dropdown only offers 'No room'

items.reasoning: No sessions were ever placed into slots, so no move/conflict-clearing/persistence step was performed or observed before the turn limit was hit.
evidence_refs: agent summary: Turn limit (70) reached before the scenario finished

items.reasoning: A 'Publish' button plus a DRAFT status badge is visible in the agenda header of both the seeded event and DevFlow Conf 2027, so a publish/go-live control clearly exists. However the agent never clicked it, so there is no evidence of a success confirmation, a status change, or the scheduled sessions appearing on any public/attendee-facing surface. Control present, handoff unverified.
evidence_refs: agent summary: Turn limit (70) reached before the scenario finished

items.reasoning: The visible agenda toolbar contains Search sessions, Group by, Send confirmations, Publish and + Add Session — no auto-schedule/AI-assist control is visible in these screenshots. However, the agent never explicitly searched for or recorded the absence of an auto-schedule capability (its explicit absence observations covered rooms/tracks only), and it ran out of turns before reaching the AIA-S2 auto-schedule step, so the evidence is not sufficient to conclude the feature is absent.
evidence_refs: agent summary: Turn limit (70) reached before the scenario finished

defects.description: No organizer-facing UI exists to create or configure agenda rooms or tracks. A newly created event (DevFlow Conf 2027) has zero rooms and zero tracks, and the Add Session dialog's Room/Track dropdowns offer only 'No room'/'No track', making room-based scheduling impossible for any non-seeded event.
defects.where: Agenda builder (Rooms view, Add Session dialog), Settings, event creation dialog

defects.description: App-wide HTTP 500 outage: after interacting with the Agenda 'Add Session' dialog, /app returned 'The server rejected the request (HTTP 500)' across dashboard, agenda and all sections, for both events, persisting across re-login. Recovery required using the homepage 'Reset demo data' option, which deleted the custom event and its data.
defects.where: /app (all sections) after Agenda Add Session interaction; recovery via homepage Reset demo data

defects.description: Workspace data tables never render for DevFlow Conf 2027: Submissions/Speakers tabs stay stuck on 'Loading…' indefinitely (across waits and reloads) despite non-zero tab badge counts; in another run the same tab returned 'Failed to load items: Failed to fetch'.
defects.where: Workspace > Submissions / Speakers tab (event-filtered to DevFlow Conf 2027)

defects.description: Off-by-one date shift in the agenda builder: day tabs/columns render 'Tue, May 11 / Wed, May 12 / Thu, May 13' while the event is configured May 12–14, 2027 (shown correctly in the sidebar), likely a timezone conversion bug.
defects.where: Agenda builder day switcher / Rooms view day columns

defects.description: Navigating to the Agenda section for DevFlow Conf 2027 intermittently returns 'The server rejected the request (HTTP 500)' instead of loading the agenda.
defects.where: Agenda section navigation

areas.notes: Both scenarios ended with agent_error at the 70-turn limit, and much of the budget was consumed by real app failures (stuck loading tables, a full HTTP 500 outage requiring a demo-data reset that deleted the fixture event). As a result the core scheduling flow (place session in a day/time/room slot, trigger speaker and room conflicts, move to resolve, reload, publish, auto-schedule) was never exercised end-to-end. Structural evidence is decent: the agenda builder with List/Day/Week/Month/Rooms/Conflicts views, day navigation, time axis, unscheduled pool, Publish button and a Conflicts counter is visible on the seeded event. The decisive functional blocker is that rooms/tracks cannot be created by an organizer, so a fresh event has no schedulable locations at all — this is a genuine app gap, not an agent failure. Downstream conflict/move/publish-handoff items lack evidence and are marked cannot_judge rather than not_found.

scenarios.scenarioName: Build agenda structure, place sessions, trigger and resolve conflicts
scenarios.summary: Turn limit (70) reached before the scenario finished.
observations: Bug: In Workspace > Submissions (and Speakers) tab for DevFlow Conf 2027 event, the data table is stuck showing "Loading row: Loading…" indefinitely (tried waiting several seconds and reloading the page) even though the tab badge shows counts (Submissions 1, Speakers 2, Messages 2). The table body never renders. This blocks viewing individual submissions here, though the counts still show non-zero, suggesting the data exists but the row-rendering component fails for this event's dataset.

Bug/quirk: Agenda builder day columns show "Tue, May 11 / Wed, May 12 / Thu, May 13" even though the event dates are configured as May 12–14, 2027 (shown correctly in the left sidebar "May 12, 2027 – May 14, 2027"). This is an off-by-one day-shift in the agenda view, likely a timezone (PDT vs UTC) conversion bug when rendering the 3 day tabs/columns.

FINDING: No UI for creating/configuring agenda Rooms or Tracks was found anywhere in the app for the DevFlow Conf 2027 event. Searched: Agenda builder (Day/Rooms/Week/Month views, "+ Add Session" dialog's Room/Track dropdowns), Settings page (only has API tokens + demo data reset), Forms admin (no field editor, only View/Copy link/Duplicate/Close/Delete), and the "Create a new event" dialog (Name/Slug/Type/Website/Location/Timezone/Dates/Description only, no rooms/tracks step). The REST API docs (/docs) also list only Events, Contacts, Submissions, Tasks, Messages, Forms resources — no Rooms/Sessions/Tracks endpoints. By contrast, the pre-seeded "AI.Engineer Sandbox Event – NYC" DOES have 6 rooms (Main Stage, Hall A, Hall B, Studio, Pavilion, Lounge) and 5 tracks (Agents, Evals, RAG & Retrieval, Infra & Serving, AI in Production) already populated, confirming these are seed-only fixtures with no organizer-facing creation UI. This means DevFlow Conf 2027, a fresh/newly-created event, has ZERO rooms and ZERO tracks available and organizers have no discovered way to add any. This is a major gap versus the scenario's expectation that "rooms are normally first configured in this area."

observations: Bug: Workspace > Submissions tab shows 'Failed to load items: Failed to fetch' error when filtered to DevFlow Conf 2027 event. This is a real error state encountered during testing.

In the Agenda 'Add session' dialog for DevFlow Conf 2027, the Track dropdown only offers 'No track' and the Room dropdown only offers 'No room' — no tracks or rooms are configured for this event, despite fixture data specifying 3 tracks and 4 rooms. This may mean event settings for tracks/rooms were not seeded, or a separate configuration step is required that wasn't discoverable here.

Bug: Navigating to Agenda section for DevFlow Conf 2027 sometimes returns 'The server rejected the request (HTTP 500)' instead of loading the agenda. Reproduced once; retrying navigation may resolve it.

Encountered a period of app-wide HTTP 500 errors on /app (dashboard, agenda, all sections, across both events) after attempting to add a session via the Agenda 'Add Session' dialog in DevFlow Conf 2027 (dialog was closed via X without submitting, since Track/Room only offered 'No track'/'No room'). The outage persisted across re-login and across switching events, suggesting a backend/global issue rather than something scoped to one event. Used the 'Reset demo data' recovery option from the homepage to restore service, as suggested by the app's own recovery messaging ('replays the seed... recreated from scratch').

After 'Reset demo data', the event filter no longer lists 'DevFlow Conf 2027' — only 'AI.Engineer Sandbox Event – NYC' remains. This confirms DevFlow Conf 2027 was a custom event (likely created during an earlier AIA-S1 run) and is NOT part of the fixed seed; resetting demo data deletes custom events. Service (HTTP 500 outage) recovered after the reset, though it's unclear if the reset itself fixed it or if it was transient and resolved with time.
